narrative.summary: A distinguished first-class passenger, Neville Fairweather, is found stabbed aboard a transatlantic ocean liner. Witnesses insist they saw Neville alive and well on the first-class promenade deck at the time of the murder, but subtle clues reveal a clever impersonation by a crew member in the steward’s uniform. The real Neville was killed elsewhere, and the false identity sighting misled the investigation until Katherine Bellamy uncovers the truth behind the disguise.

accepted_facts: Neville Fairweather’s body was found in his cabin stabbed with a stiletto dagger to the heart.
Multiple witnesses claim to have seen Neville on the first-class promenade deck around quarter to nine in the evening.
A torn piece of steward’s uniform fabric was found snagged on Neville’s cabin doorframe.
The ship’s crew schedule shows Ferdinand Carrick was in the crew quarters at the time witnesses saw Neville on the promenade deck.
A first-class passenger noted the steward Ferdinand Carrick appeared unusually nervous that evening.
inferred_conclusions: The man seen on the promenade deck was not Neville Fairweather but Ferdinand Carrick impersonating him in a steward’s uniform.
The real Neville was stabbed in his cabin earlier than the apparent time witnesses claimed to see him alive.
Ferdinand Carrick had the means, motive, and opportunity to commit the murder and stage the impersonation.

mechanism.description: Ferdinand Carrick exploited social expectations and cognitive bias by impersonating Neville Fairweather in a steward’s uniform on the restricted first-class promenade deck. Witnesses, expecting to see Neville in his customary attire, were deceived by the identical uniform and mannerisms. This role substitution concealed the true time and place of death. The ship’s crew schedule and a torn uniform fabric piece provide physical proof of the impersonation.

delivery_path.step: Ferdinand wore a steward’s uniform identical to the ship’s deck steward uniform.
He mimicked Neville’s mannerisms and gait to deceive first-class passengers.
Witness testimony placed 'Neville' on the promenade deck at quarter to nine.
A torn piece of steward’s uniform fabric found on Neville’s cabin doorframe shows the impersonation was near the victim’s cabin.
Crew schedule shows Ferdinand was not on the promenade deck at the claimed time but in the crew quarters earlier.

outcome.result: Ferdinand Carrick is identified as the murderer after disproving the false identity assumption and demonstrating the impersonation concealment.

false_assumption.statement: Witnesses correctly identified Neville Fairweather alive on the first-class promenade deck at quarter to nine.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Passengers were accustomed to seeing Neville in the first-class areas and trusted their recollections, reinforced by his distinctive dress and manner.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: That the man seen was Ferdinand Carrick, a crew member impersonating Neville in a steward’s uniform to mislead investigators and cover the real time and place of death.

supporting_points: Dr. Ashgrove had motive due to resentment and discovered secret correspondence between Lavinia and the victim.
He was near the infirmary with limited alibi and could have accessed the victim’s cabin.
His professional knowledge could explain the victim’s time of death.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: The ship’s crew schedule and witness timeline prove Dr. Ashgrove was in the infirmary during the actual time of death and could not have accessed the victim’s cabin.

red_herrings.description: A glove mark found on the stiletto dagger matched Lavinia Yardley’s glove size.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Lavinia’s glove was borrowed by a steward for cleaning the dagger display and inadvertently left a mark.

red_herrings.description: Iris Selwyn was seen arguing with Ferdinand Carrick shortly before the murder.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The argument concerned a personal dispute unrelated to the murder, resolved privately.

closed_circle.rationale: The victim was found inside his cabin on the ship, and all suspects were aboard the liner with no outsiders able to access the victim during the time window.

discriminating_test.design: A controlled inspection comparing the torn steward’s uniform fabric found on the victim’s cabin doorframe with the official uniforms issued to Ferdinand Carrick and other crew members, alongside verification of the crew schedule logs, conclusively proves that only Ferdinand’s uniform matches the torn fabric and that he was absent from the promenade deck at the time witnesses claimed to see Neville alive.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The revealed facts are assumption, promenade, and piece.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The torn fabric matches Ferdinand Carrick’s uniform only, and crew schedule logs confirm he was in the crew quarters, not the promenade deck, at the critical time.

fair_play.explanation: Step 1: The torn steward’s uniform fabric (early) and access permissions (early) expose the possibility of impersonation. Step 2: The crew schedule (mid) and witness statements reveal the contradiction in presence. Step 3: The glove mark and handling disturbance on the dagger (mid) link Ferdinand to the murder weapon. Step 4: Witness testimony of Ferdinand’s nervousness (mid) strengthens the suspicion. The discriminating test uses only these previously revealed facts to prove guilt.
